8-1.title: Drifting Continents
8-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Long ago, scientist Alfred Wegener noticed the continents look like puzzle pieces that could fit together. He proposed the idea of continental drift — that all continents were once joined in one giant supercontinent called PANGAEA and have slowly drifted apart.

Evidence for continental drift:
- Matching coastlines that fit like a puzzle (South America and Africa).
- Matching ROCKS and mountain ranges on different continents.
- Matching FOSSILS of the same plants and animals found on continents now separated by oceans.

Example 1 — Pangaea
Pangaea was the single supercontinent that contained all of today's continents joined together.

Example 2 — Fossil evidence
The same fossil found on two continents now far apart suggests they were once connected.

Example 3 — Wegener's idea
Wegener used matching coastlines, rocks, and fossils as evidence that the continents had drifted apart from Pangaea.

questions.explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed the idea of continental drift.

choices.B: Atlantis

questions.question: Continental drift is the idea that continents

choices.B: are sinking into the ocean
choices.D: have slowly moved apart over time

questions.question: Which is evidence Wegener used for continental drift?

choices.A: Matching fossils on continents now far apart
choices.B: The color of the ocean

questions.explanation: Matching fossils on now-separated continents was evidence that they were once joined.

questions.question: Why do the coastlines of South America and Africa support continental drift?

questions.explanation: The coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces, supporting the idea they were once joined.

questions.question: Finding matching mountain ranges on two separate continents suggests that they

questions.question: The same fossil of an ancient plant is found in both Africa and South America. This BEST supports the idea that

choices.A: the plant swam across the ocean
choices.B: the two continents were once connected

questions.explanation: The same fossil on both continents suggests they were once connected when the plant lived.

questions.question: Which list shows THREE types of evidence for continental drift?

choices.A: Matching coastlines, matching rocks, matching fossils
choices.B: Star maps, ocean color, wind speed

questions.explanation: Matching coastlines, rocks, and fossils are three key pieces of evidence for continental drift.

questions.question: If the continents were once joined and are now apart, then over time they have

choices.B: slowly moved away from each other

questions.explanation: Continental drift means the continents have slowly moved apart over a very long time.

questions.question: What did Wegener notice that first led him to the idea of continental drift?

choices.A: The continents look like puzzle pieces that could fit together
choices.B: The continents are all the same size

questions.explanation: Wegener noticed the continents look like puzzle pieces that could fit together, which led to his idea.

questions.question: What does the word 'drift' mean in 'continental drift'?

choices.B: To grow taller over time
choices.C: To slowly move from place to place

questions.question: Before the continents drifted apart, they were joined together as

questions.question: Which pair of continents is often used as an example because their coastlines fit together?

choices.B: Asia and Australia

questions.question: A fossil is BEST described as

choices.B: a kind of melted rock under the ocean
choices.C: a tool scientists use to measure heat

questions.explanation: A fossil is the preserved remains or trace of an ancient living thing, like a plant or animal.

questions.question: Which of these did Wegener NOT use as evidence for continental drift?

choices.C: The continents move several miles each day

questions.question: Continental drift mainly helps explain how

questions.question: Why can't a single piece of evidence, like matching coastlines, completely prove continental drift by itself?

questions.question: Which observation would a scientist studying continental drift care about MOST?

choices.B: How many birds fly over the ocean
choices.C: Matching rock layers on two separated continents

questions.question: Wegener's idea of continental drift is an example of

choices.A: a guess made with no observations at all
choices.B: a story with no connection to Earth
choices.C: a rule that can never be tested
choices.D: an explanation built from several observations and evidence

questions.question: How does the matching of fossils differ from the matching of coastlines as evidence?

questions.question: If continents are still drifting today, then in the far future the map of Earth will

choices.B: show the Sun in the center

questions.explanation: Because continents keep drifting, the future map of Earth will slowly be different from today's map.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes continental drift?

choices.B: Continents move several feet every hour
choices.C: Continents have slowly changed position over millions of years

8-2.title: Sea-Floor Spreading
8-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Deep under the oceans, hot melted rock rises up through long cracks called MID-OCEAN RIDGES. As it cools, it adds NEW rock to the sea floor and pushes the older sea floor OUTWARD on both sides.

This process is called SEA-FLOOR SPREADING. It gave scientists strong evidence for how Earth's surface moves and helped explain how continents drift apart.

Key idea: rock is YOUNGEST at the mid-ocean ridge (newest) and OLDER as you move away from the ridge.

Example 1 — New crust forms
At a mid-ocean ridge, magma rises and cools, forming new ocean floor that pushes the older floor aside.

Example 2 — Age of the sea floor
The sea floor closest to the ridge is the youngest; farther from the ridge it is older.

Example 3 — Support for drift
Sea-floor spreading explains the 'how' behind continental drift — new sea floor forming at ridges slowly moves the continents apart.

questions.question: Sea-floor spreading happens at long underwater cracks called

choices.B: sand dunes

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading happens at mid-ocean ridges, where hot melted rock rises.

questions.question: At a mid-ocean ridge, hot melted rock rises and

choices.A: cools to add new rock to the sea floor
choices.B: freezes the whole ocean

questions.explanation: The rising melted rock cools and adds new rock to the sea floor at the ridge.

questions.question: As new sea floor forms at a ridge, the older sea floor is

choices.B: pulled toward the ridge

questions.explanation: New rock at the ridge pushes the older sea floor outward on both sides.

questions.question: Where is the YOUNGEST sea-floor rock found?

choices.B: On the continents

questions.explanation: The youngest sea-floor rock is at the mid-ocean ridge, where new rock forms.

questions.question: Sea-floor rock that is FAR from a mid-ocean ridge is generally

choices.B: older than rock at the ridge

questions.explanation: Rock farther from the ridge formed earlier, so it is older than rock at the ridge.

questions.question: Sea-floor spreading helped scientists explain

choices.B: why the Sun shines

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading provided evidence for how the continents drift apart.

questions.question: Which process adds brand-new rock to Earth's surface at the bottom of the ocean?

choices.B: Sea-floor spreading

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading adds new rock to the ocean floor as magma rises and cools.

questions.question: If scientists measure rock ages across the sea floor, what pattern supports sea-floor spreading?

choices.A: Rock gets older moving away from the ridge on both sides
choices.B: Rock is the same age everywhere
choices.C: Rock gets younger far from the ridge

questions.explanation: Rock ages increasing symmetrically away from the ridge support sea-floor spreading.

questions.question: How does sea-floor spreading connect to continental drift?

choices.A: New sea floor forming at ridges slowly moves the continents apart
choices.B: It freezes the continents in place
choices.C: It has no connection at all

questions.explanation: New sea floor forming at ridges pushes plates and slowly moves the continents apart, explaining drift.

questions.question: Which statement about the mid-ocean ridge is TRUE?

choices.A: It is where the oldest rock is found
choices.B: It is where new ocean floor is created
choices.C: It is on the top of a mountain on land
choices.D: It is where the ocean is shallowest because of sand

questions.explanation: The mid-ocean ridge is where new ocean floor is created by rising, cooling magma.

questions.question: What is magma?

choices.B: Hot, melted rock

questions.explanation: Magma is hot, melted rock that rises at mid-ocean ridges.

questions.question: A mid-ocean ridge is found

choices.A: on the tops of tall land mountains
choices.B: in the center of a desert

questions.explanation: A mid-ocean ridge runs along the deep ocean floor, where new crust forms.

questions.question: When hot melted rock at a ridge cools, it

choices.B: turns into a gas and floats away

questions.explanation: When the hot melted rock cools, it hardens into solid new rock on the sea floor.

questions.question: Which describes the direction the sea floor moves during sea-floor spreading?

choices.A: It moves down into the ridge
choices.B: It moves away from the ridge on both sides
choices.D: It moves straight up to the surface

questions.explanation: During sea-floor spreading, the sea floor moves away from the ridge on both sides.

questions.question: Which list orders sea-floor rock from YOUNGEST to OLDEST?

choices.A: Rock far from the ridge, then rock near the ridge
choices.B: All rock is the same age, so there is no order
choices.C: Rock at the ridge, then rock far from the ridge
choices.D: Rock on land, then rock at the ridge

questions.explanation: Rock at the ridge is youngest and rock far from the ridge is oldest, so youngest-to-oldest goes from the ridge outward.

questions.question: Why does the sea floor get OLDER as you move away from a mid-ocean ridge?

choices.A: Because that rock formed earlier and was pushed aside as newer rock formed
choices.B: Because rock ages faster in cold water
choices.C: Because older rock floats to the surface
choices.D: Because the Sun heats it more there

questions.explanation: Rock far from the ridge formed earlier and was pushed aside as newer rock kept forming at the ridge.

questions.question: Sea-floor spreading is MOST like

choices.A: a conveyor belt carrying new rock away from the ridge
choices.B: a rock sitting still on the ground

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading works like a conveyor belt, carrying new rock outward away from the ridge.

questions.question: A scientist finds that rock 100 km east of a ridge and rock 100 km west of a ridge are about the same age. This pattern supports

choices.A: the idea that the ocean is drying up
choices.B: sea-floor spreading occurring evenly on both sides
choices.C: the idea that ridges make no new rock

questions.explanation: Matching ages at equal distances on both sides support sea-floor spreading happening evenly on both sides of the ridge.

questions.question: Which is NOT true about sea-floor spreading?

choices.A: New rock forms at mid-ocean ridges
choices.B: Rock is youngest near the ridge
choices.C: It pushes older sea floor outward
choices.D: It destroys all the rock at the ridge

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading creates new rock at the ridge and pushes older rock outward; it does not destroy all the rock at the ridge.

questions.question: Sea-floor spreading gave scientists strong evidence about how

choices.B: Earth's surface moves and continents can drift

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading gave evidence about how Earth's surface moves and how continents can drift.

questions.question: Where does the rock material that builds new sea floor come from?

choices.B: Sand carried by rivers
choices.C: Hot melted rock rising from below

questions.explanation: The new sea floor is built from hot melted rock that rises from below at the ridge and cools.

questions.question: How is the rock right at the ridge different from rock far away from the ridge?

choices.A: Rock at the ridge is younger, and rock far away is older
choices.B: Rock at the ridge is older, and rock far away is younger
choices.C: Both are exactly the same age
choices.D: Rock at the ridge is made of water

questions.explanation: Rock at the ridge is younger because it just formed, while rock far away is older.

questions.question: If sea-floor spreading suddenly stopped, what would happen to the creation of new ocean floor?

choices.A: Even more new ocean floor would form
choices.B: No new ocean floor would form at the ridge
choices.D: The ridge would turn into land

questions.explanation: If spreading stopped, no new ocean floor would form at the ridge, since spreading is what creates it.

questions.question: Which best completes this cause-and-effect statement? 'Magma rises and cools at a ridge, SO ___'

choices.A: new rock is added and the sea floor spreads
choices.B: the ocean instantly freezes

questions.explanation: Because magma rises and cools at the ridge, new rock is added and the sea floor spreads outward.

questions.question: The newest part of the ocean floor is located

choices.B: next to the continents

questions.explanation: The newest ocean floor is right at the mid-ocean ridge, where rock has just formed.

questions.question: How does sea-floor spreading support Wegener's earlier idea of continental drift?

choices.A: It proves the continents never moved
choices.B: It explains a way the continents could actually be moved apart
choices.C: It shows the continents are made of magma
choices.D: It has nothing to do with continental drift

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading explains a real way the continents could be moved apart, supporting Wegener's idea of drift.

questions.question: Which tool would be MOST useful for studying sea-floor spreading?

choices.B: A thermometer for measuring air temperature
choices.C: A device that maps the ocean floor and measures rock ages
choices.D: A telescope pointed at the stars

questions.explanation: A device that maps the ocean floor and measures rock ages directly helps study sea-floor spreading.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes what happens at a mid-ocean ridge?

choices.A: Old crust sinks back into the ridge and disappears
choices.B: Hot melted rock rises, cools, and forms new sea floor
choices.C: The ocean water boils completely away
choices.D: Sand piles up to make a mountain on land

questions.explanation: At a mid-ocean ridge, hot melted rock rises, cools, and forms new sea floor.

questions.question: Which would be the BEST evidence that the sea floor is spreading?

choices.B: All ocean rock is exactly the same color
choices.C: Rock ages increase the farther you go from the ridge on both sides

questions.explanation: Rock ages increasing the farther you go from the ridge on both sides is direct evidence the sea floor is spreading.

questions.question: In sea-floor spreading, what role does the mid-ocean ridge play?

choices.A: It is where old rock is destroyed
choices.B: It is where the ocean ends
choices.C: It is where new sea floor is made and spreading begins
choices.D: It is where continents stop moving

questions.explanation: The mid-ocean ridge is where new sea floor is made and where the spreading begins.

questions.question: Compared with rock at a mid-ocean ridge, rock found near the edge of an ocean basin is usually

choices.B: exactly the same age

questions.explanation: Rock near the edge of an ocean basin is farther from the ridge, so it is older than rock at the ridge.

questions.question: What is the MAIN idea of sea-floor spreading?

choices.B: The ocean floor is the oldest rock on Earth
choices.C: Ocean floor is made of frozen water
choices.D: New ocean floor forms at ridges and spreads outward, carrying older floor away

questions.explanation: The main idea is that new ocean floor forms at ridges and spreads outward, carrying older floor away.

questions.question: Hot melted rock is able to rise at a mid-ocean ridge because

choices.A: it is heavier than the rock around it
choices.B: it is solid and cold
choices.D: it is hot and less dense, so it rises through cracks

questions.explanation: Hot melted rock is less dense, so it rises through cracks at the ridge.

questions.question: If a piece of sea floor formed millions of years ago, where is it MOST likely now?

choices.B: Floating on the ocean surface
choices.D: Some distance away from the ridge

questions.explanation: Older sea floor has been pushed some distance away from the ridge over time.

questions.question: Which pairing of process and result is CORRECT?

choices.A: Sea-floor spreading → fossils form on land
choices.B: Sea-floor spreading → the Sun heats up
choices.D: Sea-floor spreading → new ocean floor forms

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading results in new ocean floor forming at the ridge.

questions.question: Why are mid-ocean ridges important to scientists who study Earth's changing surface?

choices.A: They show where the ocean is shallowest
choices.B: They are the warmest places in the sky
choices.C: They are where the oldest fossils are buried
choices.D: They are where new crust is constantly being made

questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges are important because they are where new crust is constantly being made.

questions.question: A model shows two halves of the sea floor moving in opposite directions away from a center line. The center line in the model represents

choices.B: the inner core

questions.explanation: The center line where new floor forms and two halves move apart represents the mid-ocean ridge.

questions.question: Which BEST explains the connection between sea-floor spreading and Earth being an active, changing planet?

choices.A: It shows the continents are shrinking into dust
choices.B: It shows Earth's surface stays frozen forever
choices.C: It shows Earth has no oceans
choices.D: It shows Earth's surface is being remade and rearranged over time

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading shows Earth's surface is being remade and rearranged over time, so Earth is active and changing.

questions.question: Which statement about new sea-floor rock is correct?

choices.A: It forms only on the continents
choices.B: It is made from ocean salt
choices.C: It is the oldest rock on the planet
choices.D: It forms at the ridge and is the youngest sea-floor rock

questions.explanation: New sea-floor rock forms at the ridge and is the youngest sea-floor rock.

questions.question: How does sea-floor spreading answer the 'HOW' that continental drift could not explain at first?

choices.A: It shows the continents are stuck and cannot move
choices.B: It shows fossils cause the movement
choices.C: It shows continents float on air
choices.D: It shows new sea floor forming at ridges can push plates and move continents apart

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading shows new sea floor forming at ridges can push plates and move continents apart, answering the 'how' of drift.

8-3.title: The Theory of Plate Tectonics
8-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Earth's crust is broken into giant pieces called TECTONIC PLATES that slowly float on the soft mantle below. They move only a few centimeters a year, but over millions of years this adds up.

Where plates meet (plate boundaries), they can:
- Push together → build mountains.
- Pull apart → open oceans / form new crust.
- Slide past each other → cause earthquakes.

These movements build mountains, open oceans, and cause earthquakes and volcanoes. This is why Earth's surface is always slowly changing.

Example 1 — Mountains form
When two plates push together, the crust crumples and pushes up, building mountains.

Example 2 — Earthquakes
When plates slide past each other, the sudden movement can cause an earthquake.

Example 3 — Slow but powerful
Plates move only a few centimeters per year — about as fast as your fingernails grow — but over millions of years they reshape Earth's surface.

questions.question: Earth's crust is broken into giant moving pieces called

choices.B: fossils

questions.explanation: Earth's crust is broken into giant pieces called tectonic plates.

questions.question: Tectonic plates slowly float on which layer of Earth?

choices.B: The inner core

questions.explanation: Tectonic plates float and move on the soft mantle below the crust.

questions.question: About how fast do tectonic plates move?

choices.B: Hundreds of miles per day
choices.D: They do not move at all

questions.explanation: Tectonic plates move only a few centimeters per year.

questions.question: When two tectonic plates push together, they can

choices.B: make the Sun shine

questions.explanation: Plates pushing together can crumple the crust and build mountains.

questions.question: Earthquakes often happen when tectonic plates

choices.B: slide past or move against each other

questions.explanation: The sudden movement of plates sliding past or against each other can cause earthquakes.

questions.question: Why is Earth's surface always slowly changing?

choices.B: Because the Sun moves

questions.explanation: The constant slow movement of tectonic plates keeps reshaping Earth's surface.

questions.question: Two plates pull apart from each other. This can

choices.A: open an ocean or form new crust
choices.B: instantly freeze the ocean

questions.explanation: When plates pull apart, new crust forms and oceans can open up in the gap.

questions.question: Volcanoes and earthquakes are MOST common

choices.A: in the middle of flat plains far from plate edges
choices.B: along the boundaries where tectonic plates meet
choices.D: only in the ocean's center, away from ridges

questions.explanation: Most volcanoes and earthquakes happen along plate boundaries where plates meet.

questions.question: Even though plates move only a few centimeters a year, they can build huge mountains because

choices.A: the movement adds up over millions of years
choices.B: they move very fast for one day
choices.C: mountains form in a single night

questions.explanation: Tiny yearly movements add up over millions of years to build huge mountains.

questions.question: Which statement BEST summarizes the theory of plate tectonics?

choices.B: Earth's crust is in giant moving plates whose motion shapes the surface
choices.C: Plates are made of liquid water
choices.D: Plates move thousands of miles each year

questions.explanation: Plate tectonics explains that Earth's crust is in giant moving plates whose slow motion shapes the surface.

questions.question: A place where two tectonic plates meet is called a

choices.B: plate boundary

questions.explanation: A place where two tectonic plates meet is called a plate boundary.

questions.question: The lesson compares the speed of plate movement to

choices.B: how fast your fingernails grow

questions.explanation: Plates move about as fast as your fingernails grow — only a few centimeters per year.

questions.question: Which layer do the tectonic plates make up?

choices.B: The ocean water

questions.explanation: The tectonic plates make up Earth's crust, the outer solid layer.

questions.question: Which event is caused by tectonic plates sliding past each other?

choices.B: An earthquake

questions.explanation: When plates slide past each other, the sudden movement can cause an earthquake.

questions.question: Which result is matched with the correct plate motion?

choices.A: Plates push together → mountains build up
choices.B: Plates push together → the ocean disappears
choices.C: Plates slide past → mountains build up
choices.D: Plates pull apart → an earthquake is impossible

questions.explanation: When plates push together, the crust crumples upward and mountains build up.

questions.question: When two plates pull apart, new crust can form. This is MOST like which ocean-floor process?

choices.B: Sea-floor spreading at a mid-ocean ridge
choices.D: Sand building up on a beach

questions.explanation: Plates pulling apart and forming new crust is like sea-floor spreading at a mid-ocean ridge.

questions.question: Which is NOT a result of moving tectonic plates?

choices.B: Earthquakes happening

questions.explanation: Moving plates build mountains, cause earthquakes, and open oceans; the Sun rising is not caused by plate motion.

questions.question: The theory of plate tectonics helps explain BOTH continental drift and sea-floor spreading because it describes

choices.A: how the whole crust is divided into moving plates
choices.B: how the Sun gives off light

questions.explanation: Plate tectonics describes how the whole crust is divided into moving plates, tying together drift and spreading.

questions.question: Why do plates move so slowly that you cannot feel it day to day?

choices.A: They move only a few centimeters per year
choices.B: They move hundreds of miles per hour
choices.C: They are stuck and never move

questions.explanation: Plates move only a few centimeters per year, far too slowly to feel day to day.

questions.question: A tall mountain range forms where two continents have collided. This is BEST explained by

choices.B: two plates pushing together

questions.explanation: Two plates pushing together can collide and crumple the crust to form tall mountains.

questions.question: What is found just below the tectonic plates that allows them to move?

choices.B: The soft, slowly flowing mantle

questions.explanation: The soft, slowly flowing mantle lies below the plates and allows them to move.

questions.question: Which list shows THREE things plate movements can cause?

choices.B: Rainbows, sunsets, and clouds

questions.explanation: Plate movements can build mountains and cause earthquakes and volcanoes.

questions.question: How is plate tectonics different from the earlier idea of continental drift?

choices.A: Plate tectonics describes the moving plates that explain HOW the continents move, not just THAT they move
choices.B: They are exactly the same idea with no difference
choices.C: Plate tectonics says continents never move
choices.D: Continental drift describes plates and tectonics describes fossils

questions.explanation: Plate tectonics goes further than continental drift by describing the moving plates that explain how the continents move.

questions.question: A region has frequent earthquakes and volcanoes. A scientist would predict that this region is

choices.B: located near a boundary where plates meet
choices.C: in the exact center of a plate

questions.explanation: Frequent earthquakes and volcanoes are signs the region is located near a boundary where plates meet.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes tectonic plates?

choices.B: They are made of ocean water
choices.C: They are giant pieces of Earth's crust that slowly move
choices.D: They are tiny pieces smaller than a grain of sand

questions.explanation: Tectonic plates are giant pieces of Earth's crust that slowly move.

questions.question: When plates pull apart on the ocean floor, the gap is filled by

choices.B: blowing sand from a desert
choices.C: new crust forming as melted rock rises and cools

questions.explanation: When plates pull apart on the ocean floor, new crust forms as melted rock rises and cools.

questions.question: Over millions of years, the slow motion of plates can

choices.B: make the surface freeze solid forever

questions.explanation: Over millions of years, the slow motion of plates can completely reshape Earth's surface.

questions.question: Which type of plate boundary is matched with the WRONG result?

choices.B: Plates pulling apart → opening oceans
choices.D: Plates sliding past → making the Sun brighter

questions.explanation: Plates sliding past each other cause earthquakes; they do not make the Sun brighter, so that pairing is wrong.

questions.question: The theory of plate tectonics is important because it

choices.A: tells us the weather for tomorrow
choices.B: explains how stars are made
choices.C: explains many of Earth's features and events with one big idea

questions.explanation: Plate tectonics is important because one big idea explains many of Earth's features and events, like mountains and earthquakes.

questions.question: If tectonic plates suddenly stopped moving forever, which would MOST likely happen?

choices.A: All rivers would dry up instantly
choices.B: The Sun would stop shining
choices.C: New mountains and ocean basins would stop forming from plate motion

questions.explanation: If plates stopped moving, new mountains and ocean basins would stop forming from plate motion.

questions.question: Which best describes a plate boundary?

choices.A: The center of a flat plain
choices.B: The middle of the ocean far from any plate
choices.C: The edge where one plate meets another plate
choices.D: The top layer of the atmosphere

questions.explanation: A plate boundary is the edge where one plate meets another plate.

questions.question: Two plates that push together cause the crust to

choices.B: spread flat and disappear
choices.C: crumple and push up into mountains

questions.explanation: When plates push together, the crust crumples and pushes up into mountains.

questions.question: How does the theory of plate tectonics connect to sea-floor spreading?

choices.A: Plate tectonics only happens on land, never in the ocean
choices.B: They are not connected in any way
choices.C: Sea-floor spreading stops plates from moving
choices.D: Sea-floor spreading is one way plate boundaries form new crust as plates pull apart

questions.explanation: Sea-floor spreading is one way plate boundaries form new crust as plates pull apart, so it fits within plate tectonics.

questions.question: Which statement about plate movement is TRUE?

choices.A: Plates move thousands of miles each year
choices.B: Plates never change Earth's surface
choices.C: Plates only move during the day
choices.D: Plates move a few centimeters each year, but the effects add up over time

questions.explanation: Plates move only a few centimeters each year, but the effects add up over a very long time.

questions.question: Why can plate tectonics be called a 'theory' in science?

choices.A: It is a wild guess with no support
choices.B: It is just a story people made up for fun
choices.D: It is a well-supported explanation backed by lots of evidence

questions.explanation: In science, plate tectonics is a theory because it is a well-supported explanation backed by lots of evidence.

questions.question: An ocean slowly grows wider over millions of years. This is BEST explained by plates that are

choices.B: sliding sideways past each other

questions.explanation: An ocean growing wider is best explained by plates pulling apart, which opens the ocean and forms new crust.

questions.question: Which is the BEST evidence that Earth's surface is still changing today?

choices.A: The Moon changes shape in the sky
choices.B: The Sun rises every morning
choices.D: Earthquakes and volcanoes still happen along plate boundaries

questions.explanation: Earthquakes and volcanoes still happening along plate boundaries are evidence Earth's surface is still changing.

questions.question: Which correctly orders the size relationship?

choices.A: A tectonic plate is smaller than a single rock
choices.B: A tectonic plate is smaller than a grain of sand
choices.C: A tectonic plate and a pebble are the same size
choices.D: A tectonic plate is much larger than a single mountain

questions.explanation: Tectonic plates are giant pieces of crust, so a plate is much larger than a single mountain.

questions.question: What MAIN idea ties together drifting continents, sea-floor spreading, and plate tectonics?

choices.B: Earth's surface is frozen and never changes
choices.C: The Sun controls all of Earth's rocks
choices.D: Earth's surface is made of moving plates that slowly reshape the planet

questions.explanation: The main idea tying these lessons together is that Earth's surface is made of moving plates that slowly reshape the planet.

questions.question: A student wants to predict where the next big earthquake might strike. The BEST place to look is

choices.A: in the flat center of a large plate
choices.B: high in the clouds
choices.C: in the deepest part of a calm desert
choices.D: near a plate boundary where plates meet and move

questions.explanation: Earthquakes are most common near plate boundaries where plates meet and move, so that is the best place to predict one.
